scenario.title: SMT line with dense telemetry and serialized boards
scenario.story: Every SMT line has a reflow profile that looks fine on paper and misbehaves at 4 pm. Acme's SMT line feeds serialized Sensor PCB v3 boards into automotive assemblies, where traceability to component lot is a customer requirement. Cross-line telemetry is missing and the serial number-to-defect link is manual today, which means a defect traced back to a component lot becomes a fire drill. This demo shows a data-rich line view with solder paste temperatures, pick-and-place cycle counts, reflow oven profile, and AOI reject rates all visible in a single monitoring POD. An automotive quality auditor watches the reflow oven trend break its control limit and DM flag the affected serial range automatically. Without DM, the serial-to-defect link stays manual and the first signal of a lot problem is a customer complaint.
scenario.rework_rationale: No signals fired: focus does not include quality-rework, no quality pain points at medium+ confidence.

moments_of_expertise.evidence: Thermal drift in reflow ovens is a documented failure mode; the demo surfaces it in the monitoring POD.

moments_of_expertise.claim: Serial traceability is only valuable when a defect happens, so build it before you need it.
moments_of_expertise.evidence: Automotive customer requires lot-level traceability; current manual link is a risk.
